key_insight: The paper shows that distributed quantum circuit execution can be made classically tractable by exploiting a weakly coupled qubit to approximate circuit "knitting" with polynomial overhead.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable distributed quantum computing workflows by trading exactness for controlled approximation, which is attractive for near-term hardware constraints and circuit partitioning.
method: Partition the quantum procedure around a qubit that is weakly coupled to the rest of the system.
Use a weak-coupling approximation to reconstruct the distributed process with reduced classical cost.
Demonstrate the approach on a layered circuit inspired by QAOA-style circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that exact reconstruction needs exponential classical information, while the proposed approximation reduces the classical cost to polynomial and is demonstrated on layered QAOA-like circuits.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the validity of the weak-coupling assumption, so performance may degrade when inter-qubit coupling is not sufficiently small.
paper_title: Scalable quantum circuit knitting using a weak-coupling approximation
